candidates.explanation: Pipeline-aware relaxation: reduce orders when pipeline is high and inventory is low, to avoid over-ordering and upstream backlog. For node0, if pipeline > 10 and inventory < 5, reduce order by 2. For node1, if pipeline > 10 and inventory < 2, reduce by 3. For node2, if pipeline > 5 and inventory < 5, reduce by 2.

Backlog-driven increase: if backlog exists, increase order to replenish, but cap to avoid over-ordering. For node0, if backlog > 0, increase by 1. For node1, if backlog > 0, increase by 2. For node2, if backlog > 0, increase by 1.

Demand-growth response: if recent demand exceeds baseline (growth > 1.1), increase orders to meet potential emergency, but only if inventory is not excessive. For node0, if growth > 1.1 and inventory < 10, increase by 2. For node1, if growth > 1.1 and inventory < 5, increase by 3. For node2, if growth > 1.1 and inventory < 10, increase by 2.

Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.
Expression features ONLY: agent, inventory, backlog, pipeline=sum of known in-transit, arrival=next known arrival, incoming=last observed local demand, recent=last5 external mean, baseline=preceding20 external mean, growth=recent/baseline, happo=current proposed order.
Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. This synchronous30-second HTTP timeout is not a real-world execution deadline guarantee.

agent==1 and backlog==0 and inventory>15 and growth>1.05
agent==2 and backlog==0 and inventory>20 and growth>1.05

rules.when: agent==1 and backlog==0 and inventory<10 and growth>1.1

candidates.explanation: Pipeline-aware smoothing: if pipeline is high relative to recent demand, reduce orders to avoid excess inventory; if pipeline is low and demand is growing, increase orders to prevent stockouts.

rules.when: agent==0 and pipeline<recent and growth>1.1 and backlog==0

candidates.explanation: Modest pipeline-aware relaxation: reduce orders when pipeline is high relative to recent demand, increase when inventory is low and pipeline is low. Coordinated across nodes to avoid starvation.

Stronger pipeline-aware relaxation: more aggressive reduction when pipeline exceeds 6 times recent demand, and increase when inventory is very low and pipeline is low. Backlog triggers small increase.

Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.
Expression features ONLY: agent, inventory, backlog, pipeline=sum of known in-transit, arrival=next known arrival, incoming=last observed local demand, recent=last5 external mean, baseline=preceding20 external mean, growth=recent/baseline, happo=current proposed order.
Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. This synchronous30-second HTTP timeout is not a real-world execution deadline guarantee.

Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.
Expression features ONLY: agent, inventory, backlog, pipeline=sum of known in-transit, arrival=next known arrival, incoming=last observed local demand, recent=last5 external mean, baseline=preceding20 external mean, growth=recent/baseline, happo=current proposed order.
Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. This synchronous30-second HTTP timeout is not a real-world execution deadline guarantee.

candidates.explanation: Pipeline-aware relaxation: when inventory is zero and backlog is high, reduce orders to avoid worsening upstream backlog, but only if pipeline is sufficient to cover near-term demand. For node0, high backlog and pipeline indicate demand is being met; reduce order to prevent over-ordering. For upstream nodes, reduce orders when their backlog is low and pipeline is high, to avoid creating upstream backlog.

rules.when: agent==0 and inventory==0 and backlog>50 and pipeline>=40
agent==1 and inventory==0 and backlog<20 and pipeline>=40
agent==2 and inventory==0 and backlog<10 and pipeline>=40

candidates.explanation: Coordinated backlog reduction: when downstream backlog is high, upstream nodes should not increase orders to avoid starving downstream. Node0 increases order slightly to replenish, but node1 and node2 reduce orders if their backlog is low and pipeline is high, ensuring pipeline flow to node0.

rules.when: agent==1 and inventory==0 and backlog<15 and pipeline>=50
agent==2 and inventory==0 and backlog<5 and pipeline>=50

candidates.explanation: Demand growth response: if recent demand exceeds baseline (growth>1.1), increase orders at all nodes to build inventory, but cap increases to avoid overshoot. If growth is moderate, keep orders steady. This helps meet emergency demand without causing excessive backlog.

messages.content:
Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.
Expression features ONLY: agent, inventory, backlog, pipeline=sum of known in-transit, arrival=next known arrival, incoming=last observed local demand, recent=last5 external mean, baseline=preceding20 external mean, growth=recent/baseline, happo=current proposed order.
Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. This synchronous30-second HTTP timeout is not a real-world execution deadline guarantee.
